title: Finite scalar mates as maps of coherent coefficient systems
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\pi,v$, and a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $A_n=R/\pi^n$, $B_n=S/\pi^nS=S/v^{en}$, where $e$ is the ramification index. Work on fixed small pro-etale skeletons with completed coefficient sheaves $\widehat R_W,\widehat S_W$ and bounded derived-complete constructible categories $\mathcal C_R(W),\mathcal C_S(W)$ for $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Let $T_W=-\widehat\otimes_R^L S$ be the prescribed strict-tower scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and $T_{W,n}=-\otimes_{A_n}^LB_n$. Use the constructible adjunctions $F_R=Rf_{!,R}\dashv G_R=Rf_R^!$ and $F_S\dashv G_S$, with units $\eta_R,\eta_S$ and counits $\varepsilon_R,\varepsilon_S$, as realized by [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. Fix one compactification of $f$ for these functors [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Let $\alpha:T_YF_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_ST_X$ be the compact-support scalar comparison obtained by total inverse limit of the finite-free comparisons $\alpha_n:T_{Y,n}F_{A_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{B_n}T_{X,n}$: on a basis of the finite free $R$-module $S$ they are finite-sum distributivity. Use the canonical completed-scalar comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] when commuting $T$ with total limit. For $M\in\mathcal C_R(Y)$, put $M_n=M\otimes^L_{\widehat R_Y}(A_n)_Y$. The finite exceptional comparison $b_{n,M_n}:T_{X,n}G_{A_n}M_n\to G_{B_n}T_{Y,n}M_n$ is the transpose of
$$F_{B_n}T_{X,n}G_{A_n}M_n\xrightarrow{\alpha_{n,G_{A_n}M_n}^{-1}}T_{Y,n}F_{A_n}G_{A_n}M_n\xrightarrow{T_{Y,n}\varepsilon_{A_n,M_n}}T_{Y,n}M_n.$$
In the simultaneous derived coefficient-system realizations of [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization, lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], these finite transposes define a natural morphism of normalized derived $B_n$-coefficient systems, with quotient transitions those of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] and the finite-free coefficient squares of [lem-coef-finite-free-extension]. This is the coherent transpose on those system realizations, rather than a lift chosen only by its finite evaluations. Its total derived inverse limit, under the specified comparisons of source with $T_XG_RM$ and target with $G_ST_YM$, is the $F_S\dashv G_S$ transpose of
$$F_ST_XG_RM\xrightarrow{\alpha_{G_RM}^{-1}}T_YF_RG_RM\xrightarrow{T_Y\varepsilon_{R,M}}T_YM.$$
The equality is an equality of the natural integral maps obtained from the specified system realizations.

proof.text: For $M\in\mathcal C_R(Y)$, the residue-Tor result gives a uniform finite Tor interval for $N=\mathcal R_{R,Y}M$. Apply the ramified scalar-system transpose construction to $N$. Its specified $\alpha^{\rm sys}$ evaluates to the given finite-free $\alpha_n$, and its $b^{\rm sys}_N$ evaluates to the displayed finite transposes, with the required exceptional quotient cocycle and finite-free coefficient squares. In particular this is an actual natural map of normalized systems, constructed by simultaneous transposition.

source.place: paragraph 8, first and third sentences: finite-free compact-support tensor and transposition; extracted returned steps 1–4

proof.text: Apply the cofinal scalar exceptional-limit realization to $M$. It supplies the specified natural identifications of the limit source with $T_XG_RM$ and target with $G_ST_YM$, and identifies the limit of $\alpha^{\rm sys}$ with $\alpha$. The Tor intervals, constructibility and cofinal $en$-tower comparisons required for these applications are part of that result. Applying total derived limit to $b^{\rm sys}_N$ therefore gives a natural integral map $b:T_XG_RM\to G_ST_YM$.

source.place: paragraph 8, first sentence: finite free tensor commutes with the derived limit defining integral compact support; extracted returned steps 5–6

proof.text: The system transpose identity is $\epsilon^{\rm sys}_{S,\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}N}\circ\mathsf F_S(b^{\rm sys}_N)=\lambda_N$. Apply normalized reconstruction adjunction calculus to the constructible normalized $S$-systems: under its actual unit/counit identifications the integral adjunct of $b$ is $\mathcal L_{S,Y}^{(e)}(\lambda_N)$. The scalar-counit limit result identifies this map with $T_Y(\varepsilon_{R,M})\circ\alpha_{G_RM}^{-1}$. Thus $b$ is precisely the required integral transpose. Every identification is natural in $M$, so this is the claimed equality of specified natural integral maps. The equality is obtained from the system transpose identity, without inferring it from equality of finite projections.
